findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — Credential-sync refresh returns a Fetch Response but this path reads its nonexistent `.data`, so every synced Google token refresh fails before persistence.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:101 — The newly refreshed Salesforce token is persisted but the connection is built with the stale pre-refresh access token, causing the current request to fail after a refresh.
packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The credential-sync fetch has no timeout, so an unavailable sync service can indefinitely stall every affected calendar refresh.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — The shared helper erases its return contract with `any` even though sync mode returns a Fetch Response and normal mode returns provider-specific token objects.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The credential-sync fetch has no timeout, so an unavailable sync service can indefinitely stall every affected calendar refresh.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the refreshOAuthTokens function in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts, the fetch call to process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no timeout configuration. The fetch API in Node.js doesn't have a default timeout, so if the sync service is unavailable or slow, this could indeed block indefinitely. This is a real operational concern - if APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and the endpoint is configured but unresponsive, calendar refresh operations would hang. This is a legitimate defect in the new code being added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — The shared helper erases its return contract with `any` even though sync mode returns a Fetch Response and normal mode returns provider-specific token objects.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for refreshOAuthTokens.ts, the function signature is `async (refreshFunction: () => any, appSlug: string, userId: number | null)` and returns `Promise<any>`. The function either calls the external sync endpoint (returning a fetch Response) or calls the provided refreshFunction (which returns whatever the caller's refresh logic returns). This is a real type safety issue - the return type is `any` which erases type information, and the two code paths return fundamentally different types (fetch Response vs provider-specific token objects). Callers like GoogleCalendarService expect `res?.data.access_token` but if the sync endpoint is used, they'd get a raw Response object instead. This is a genuine correctness/type safety problem in the implementation.
